requirements.text: Implement global FIFO service in acceptance order, including same-address writes and reads. Admit on every rising-edge txn_valid && txn_ready, independently of command readiness.
requirements.verification:
source: system.rules.R1
origin: request.R1
obligations:
  V_R1:
    rules:
    - R1
    scenario: Apply consecutive valid requests, including same-address writes followed
      by reads, while command progress varies independently.
    expected: Each qualifying ready/valid edge admits one request; service and final
      completion remain in acceptance order; cmd_ready does not affect admission.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Provide four waiting entries plus one separately stored active request. Dispatch only previously stored requests, capture the complete pre-edge head before releasing its slot, and permit full-queue simultaneous dispatch/admission including capacity one. No empty-queue bypass or same-edge active replacement at retirement.
requirements.verification:
source: system.rules.R2
origin: request.R2
obligations:
  V_R2:
    rules:
    - R2
    scenario: Exercise empty, partial, and full waiting storage, including capacity
      one and simultaneous dispatch/admission.
    expected: Only pre-edge stored entries dispatch; the pre-edge head is captured
      before release; no bypass or retirement-edge active replacement occurs.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Use explicit NOP/ACT/PRE/READ/WRITE/REF command semantics, with NOP never committed and at most one command commit per edge. Sequence closed banks with ACT-access, row hits with access, and row conflicts with PRE-ACT-access. PRE/ACT never retire the active request. Keep blocked candidates stable through stalls and newly pending refresh.
requirements.verification:
source: system.rules.R3
origin: request.R3
obligations:
  V_R3:
    rules:
    - R3
    scenario: Service closed-bank, row-hit, and row-conflict reads and writes while
      timing-blocking each candidate and raising refresh pending.
    expected: Only NOP, ACT, PRE, READ, WRITE, and REF semantics are used; one command
      at most commits per edge; setup does not retire; blocked candidates remain stable.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Keep separate owners for host mapping, waiting storage, scheduling, command sequencing, row state, timing, functional memory/responses, and refresh control. The top must contain structural connections only.
requirements.verification:
source: system.rules.R4
origin: request.R4
obligations:

    expected: Required behavioral roles are independently contractable with structural
      top-level integration only; no single owner contract contains all required functions.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Update bank state and timing history only from committed commands. Enforce tRCD, tRAS, tRP, tRRD, tFAW and tRFC using the selected project profile. A trigger at E permits the blocked command at E+T; tFAW counts earlier ACT commits with age strictly less than its window. Reset creates no synthetic timing history.
requirements.verification:
source: system.rules.R5
origin: request.R5
obligations:
  V_R5:
    rules:
    - R5
    scenario: Test each timing relation at E+T-1 and E+T, including reset, ACT bursts,
      and REF exclusion.
    expected: Only committed history changes timing and bank state; tRCD, tRAS, tRP,
      tRRD, tFAW, and tRFC use the selected profile and exact edge convention.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Preserve functional banked 32-bit memory and compact host address mapping. WRITE commit updates storage; READ commit at E captures pre-edge data and registers valid/data for host sampling at E+1, with no extra adapter response register. Responses survive active release, cleanup and refresh; writes produce no response.
requirements.verification:
source: system.rules.R6
origin: request.R6
obligations:
  V_R6:
    rules:
    - R6
    scenario: Write distinct values to all compact addresses in multiple banks, read
      them, and reset during response visibility.
    expected: Only committed WRITE changes addressed banked storage; READ captures
      pre-edge data and produces one E+1 response; responses survive active release
      and refresh.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Open-page retains rows. Support close-page as a configurable alternative, retaining a separate cleanup bank reservation after retirement until a legal PRE commits; block new dispatch during cleanup.

source: system.rules.R7

obligations:

    scenario: Run identical traffic under open_page and close_page parameter values.
    expected: Open-page retains serviced rows; close-page reserves cleanup until legal
      PRE and blocks dispatch during cleanup.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Generate periodic refresh deadlines from the last sampled reset edge using tREFI. Coalesce missed deadlines into sticky pending; a due deadline wins over simultaneous REF acknowledgment. Drain active work and cleanup, PRE remaining open banks in ascending order, respect all-bank tRP, commit REF once, and exclude commands strictly before REF-edge+tRFC. Retain queued traffic and resume service afterward.
requirements.verification:
source: system.rules.R8
origin: request.R8
obligations:
  V_R8:
    rules:
    - R8
    scenario: Create refresh due conditions while idle, active, cleanup-reserved,
      and during refresh service; leave multiple banks open.
    expected: Pending coalesces, due wins over simultaneous acknowledgment, active
      and cleanup drain before ascending PRE, REF commits once, tRFC exclusion holds,
      and queued traffic resumes.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: cmd_ready is reset-gated diagnostic readiness for the incoming request's first needed command, using independent row/timing probe queries while the engine is idle and cleanup/refresh permit. It is meaningful without txn_valid and must not admit, dispatch, bypass FIFO, mutate history or reserve storage.

obligations:

      state, cleanup, refresh, and txn_valid.
    expected: cmd_ready reports only the defined first-command diagnostic probe and
      never changes admission, storage, dispatch, history, or reservations.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Use synchronous active-low reset for state, with immediate valid/ready/event gating. Reset clears queued/active/cleanup work, row state, timing history, memory, responses and refresh state; it wins over every simultaneous event. The host holds payload while stalled and samples every response; no response backpressure is provided.

obligations:

    scenario: Assert reset during queued, active, stalled, refresh, command-commit,
      and response conditions.
    expected: Reset immediately gates visible valid, ready, and events low and synchronously
      clears specified state at the sampled edge; no pre-reset work reappears.
    status: planned_not_executed

Export it alongside RTL for the external UVM/vector stage. Do not execute downstream verification or backend stages in this frontend flow.

Consecutive accepted cycles with txn_valid held high are distinct requests. cmd_ready is execution/timing visibility, not the host acceptance handshake. Deassert txn_ready and rsp_valid during reset.

Preserve explicit txn_bank for multi-bank configurations; a single-bank configuration uses bank 0. Internal packed requests retain bank(2), row(10), column(6), write flag(1), write data(32).

requirements.text: Provide 4 WAITING request slots PLUS one separately stored active-service request: waiting plus active capacity is 5. The active request must not consume a waiting slot. Dispatch captures the complete pre-edge request in active registers and frees its waiting slot without retiring the transaction. A full queue may admit on the same edge as dispatch; retirement alone does not free waiting storage. Accepted request fields survive stalls and each accepted request is serviced exactly once within a reset-free epoch. Keep admission, dispatch, retirement and read response delivery distinct. Captured response storage consumes neither waiting nor active capacity.
requirements.verification:
source: system.rules.BASE_QUEUE
origin: request.BASE_QUEUE
obligations:
  V_BASE_QUEUE:
    rules:
    - BASE_QUEUE
    scenario: Fill waiting storage while one active request stalls, then perform dispatch/admission,
      retirement, and read response delivery independently.
    expected: Four waiting plus one active request are retained; dispatch frees waiting
      storage but not transaction ownership; response storage consumes neither capacity.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Provide functional 32-bit memory storage with 16 addresses per bank, bank isolation and reset-to-zero contents. Accepted writes update only their addressed location at service completion or a committed WRITE. Each accepted read produces exactly one one-cycle rsp_valid pulse with the stored rsp_rdata after read service/READ commit, using the existing one-cycle response stage. Writes produce no host response. Selection and stalled candidates cannot mutate memory; mere command output without storage and read responses is insufficient.
requirements.verification:
source: system.rules.BASE_DATA
origin: request.BASE_DATA
obligations:
  V_BASE_DATA:
    rules:

    scenario: Scoreboard bank-isolated writes and reads over all sixteen locations
      per bank and inject blocked proposals.
    expected: Reset data are zero; only committed writes update data; every committed
      read yields exactly one response; proposals do not mutate storage.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Retain existing tRCD, tRAS and tRP timing protection from the selected JEDEC profile. ACT-to-READ/WRITE must wait tRCD, ACT-to-PRE must respect tRAS, and PRE-to-next-ACT must respect tRP if explicit commands are used. Aggregate service may retain the existing protected timing envelope instead. Configured tRRD and tFAW gates must use accepted activation events, not host admissions or stalled proposals. Never treat existing basic timing as an unrequested future feature.

source: system.rules.BASE_TIMING

      activation commits rather than admissions or proposals.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Dispatch captures the complete selected request in separate active-service registers before freeing its waiting queue slot. Hold that active request and payload across setup PRE/ACT and timing stalls until its final READ/WRITE commits. Setup commands never retire the active request. Aggregate service also keeps active-service ownership through completion. Waiting-queue dequeue at dispatch is distinct from active-request retirement. Row state changes only on the responsible committed operation; uncommitted proposals cannot change state.

    expected: Captured active payload survives until final commit; dispatch/dequeue
      and retirement remain distinct; only committed operations change row state.
    status: planned_not_executed

No single controller core may own all these functions. Each mandatory role has distinct module owners with functional inter-module connections. requirements.text: Compute command permission from registered timing/bank history and an independent candidate. An accepted ACT pulse is derived from candidate && permission; permission must not combinationally depend on that same accepted pulse. Scheduler selection/validity must be available independently of timing_ok; timing_ok may gate commit but must not create a selection-validity feedback loop. Declare accurate per-output combinational input dependencies.

requirements.text: Acceptance order defines global FIFO order. Dispatch transfers only the oldest previously stored request. Physical row state, legality, cleanup, refresh, and timing may delay service but may not select a younger request ahead of the oldest waiting request.

requirements.text: At a reset edge, reset wins over admission, dispatch, command commit, retirement, response delivery, refresh due, and refresh acknowledgment. Without reset, a full waiting queue may admit and dispatch on the same edge using the pre-edge head and pre-edge incoming payload. Retirement does not authorize dispatch on its own edge. A refresh due coincident with REF commit leaves refresh pending set for a later service interval.

source: system.rules.SYS_SIMULTANEOUS
origin: model_selected
obligations:
  V_SYS_SIMULTANEOUS:
    rules:
    - SYS_SIMULTANEOUS
    scenario: Align reset, full-queue admission/dispatch, retirement, refresh due,
      and REF commit in separate and combined trials.
    expected: Specified priority and same-edge outcomes occur with no lost request,
      duplicate request, or lost refresh due.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Waiting storage, active-service storage, and captured response storage are logically distinct capacities. Active-service storage contains one complete dispatched request until final READ or WRITE commit. Captured response storage contains no request-capacity claim and survives active release, cleanup, and refresh service.
requirements.verification:
source: system.rules.SYS_STORAGE_OWNERSHIP
origin: model_selected
obligations:
  V_SYS_STORAGE_OWNERSHIP:
    rules:
    - SYS_STORAGE_OWNERSHIP
    scenario: Track waiting, active, and response occupancy through dispatch, retirement,
      cleanup, refresh, and response delivery.
    expected: The three storage categories remain capacity-independent as specified.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Exactly one non-NOP command may commit at a rising edge. Closed-bank service requires ACT then READ or WRITE; matching open-row service requires READ or WRITE; conflicting open-row service requires PRE then ACT then READ or WRITE. PRE and ACT are setup commands and never retire active service. Candidate payload remains stable while blocked, including when refresh becomes pending.
requirements.verification:
source: execution.rules.EXEC_COMMANDS
origin: model_selected
obligations:
  V_EXEC_COMMANDS:
    rules:
    - EXEC_COMMANDS
    scenario: Run closed, hit, and conflict sequences with multi-cycle timing stalls
      and refresh pending transitions.
    expected: Committed trace is ACT-access, access, or PRE-ACT-access as applicable;
      setup never retires and no candidate changes while blocked.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Candidate selection and validity are independently available before timing permission. Permission is computed from registered bank and timing history and the independent candidate. ACT acceptance equals ACT candidate and permission, but permission has no combinational dependency on the accepted ACT pulse or on same-edge committed command outputs.
requirements.verification:
source: execution.rules.EXEC_PERMISSION
origin: model_selected
obligations:
  V_EXEC_PERMISSION:
    rules:
    - EXEC_PERMISSION
    scenario: Probe permission with fixed registered history while varying candidate
      and compare against stalled and accepted ACT behavior.
    expected: Candidate validity remains independently observable; permission is history-based
      and acceptance feedback-free.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Only committed ACT sets the target bank valid and row, committed PRE clears the target bank validity, and committed REF leaves all banks closed after required preparation. READ and WRITE do not alter row state. Proposals, admissions, dispatch, timing probes, and stalled candidates do not alter row state.
requirements.verification:
source: execution.rules.EXEC_BANK_STATE
origin: model_selected
obligations:

    rules:
    - EXEC_BANK_STATE
    scenario: Commit ACT, PRE, READ, WRITE, and REF in multiple banks and separately
      issue uncommitted proposals.
    expected: Only responsible committed commands change only permitted bank-state
      fields.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: For PAGE_POLICY=open_page, final READ or WRITE retirement retains the serviced row. For PAGE_POLICY=close_page, retirement creates a separate cleanup reservation for the serviced bank; no new dispatch occurs until the required timing-legal PRE commits. Cleanup does not repeat retirement or response delivery.
requirements.verification:
source: execution.rules.EXEC_CLEANUP
origin: model_selected
obligations:
  V_EXEC_CLEANUP:
    rules:
    - EXEC_CLEANUP
    scenario: Retire accesses under both page policies and raise refresh during close-page
      cleanup.
    expected: Open-page retains rows; close-page reserves cleanup and blocks dispatch
      until PRE commits without duplicate retirement or response.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: At READ commit edge E, response storage captures the addressed pre-edge memory word and rsp_valid is asserted after E. The host samples that response at E+1. In the absence of replacement, rsp_valid clears after the delivery edge while rsp_rdata may retain its last value. A delivery and a new READ commit may share an edge: old response data is delivered before new response state replaces it. WRITE produces no response.
requirements.verification:
source: execution.rules.EXEC_RESPONSE
origin: model_selected
obligations:
  V_EXEC_RESPONSE:
    rules:
    - EXEC_RESPONSE
    scenario: Commit reads on adjacent edges, read after writes, issue writes, and
      reset during a response pulse.
    expected: Each read returns captured pre-edge data exactly once at E+1, writes
      return no response, and old data is delivered before same-edge replacement.
    status: planned_not_executed

requirements.text: Refresh deadlines are measured from the last sampled reset edge. The first due edge is E0+tREFI and later deadlines advance by tREFI independently of REF commit. Pending is sticky and coalesces later due edges. Once pending is visible, no new dispatch occurs; active service and required cleanup complete, then open banks PRE in ascending bank order, respecting timing. REF commits once after all banks are closed and all-bank tRP is satisfied. Commands are excluded at candidate edges strictly before REF-edge+tRFC; queued traffic remains retained and resumes after service when no pending refresh remains.

system.verification.V_BASE_HOST.scenario: Hold valid high across ready cycles and hold payload stable across stalls and reset.
system.verification.V_BASE_HOST.expected: Ports and widths match; each ready/valid edge is distinct; txn_ready and rsp_valid are low during reset; cmd_ready is not an acceptance handshake.

system.verification.V_BASE_ADDRESS.scenario: Apply every 4-bit address and all four banks.
system.verification.V_BASE_ADDRESS.expected: Rows and columns are zero-extended from the specified address slices; internal request fields retain bank, row, column, write flag, and data.

system.verification.V_BASE_RESET.scenario: Check top clock/reset polarity and reset behavior across all state categories.
system.verification.V_BASE_RESET.expected: clk/rst_n polarity is preserved, synchronous reset clears required state, and no polarity adapter is required.

system.verification.V_R1.scenario: Apply consecutive valid requests, including same-address writes followed by reads, while command progress varies independently.
system.verification.V_R1.expected: Each qualifying ready/valid edge admits one request; service and final completion remain in acceptance order; cmd_ready does not affect admission.

system.verification.V_R9.scenario: Vary incoming address, row state, timing legality, queue fullness, idle/busy state, cleanup, refresh, and txn_valid.
system.verification.V_R9.expected: cmd_ready reports only the defined first-command diagnostic probe and never changes admission, storage, dispatch, history, or reservations.

system.verification.V_R10.scenario: Assert reset during queued, active, stalled, refresh, command-commit, and response conditions.
system.verification.V_R10.expected: Reset immediately gates visible valid, ready, and events low and synchronously clears specified state at the sampled edge; no pre-reset work reappears.

system.verification.V_R11.scenario: Review generated future verification intent against all rule IDs and declared host/event bindings.
system.verification.V_R11.expected: Every request rule has reciprocal planned verification, declared independent scenarios, and expected outcomes; no downstream execution claim is made.

system.verification.V_CONSTRAINT_8.scenario: Inspect timing profile selection and command vocabulary.

system.verification.V_BASE_QUEUE.scenario: Fill waiting storage while one active request stalls, then perform dispatch/admission, retirement, and read response delivery independently.
system.verification.V_BASE_QUEUE.expected: Four waiting plus one active request are retained; dispatch frees waiting storage but not transaction ownership; response storage consumes neither capacity.

system.verification.V_R2.scenario: Exercise empty, partial, and full waiting storage, including capacity one and simultaneous dispatch/admission.
system.verification.V_R2.expected: Only pre-edge stored entries dispatch; the pre-edge head is captured before release; no bypass or retirement-edge active replacement occurs.

system.verification.V_CONSTRAINT_11.scenario: Fill waiting storage under the selected configuration.

system.verification.V_SYS_SIMULTANEOUS.scenario: Align reset, full-queue admission/dispatch, retirement, refresh due, and REF commit in separate and combined trials.
system.verification.V_SYS_SIMULTANEOUS.expected: Specified priority and same-edge outcomes occur with no lost request, duplicate request, or lost refresh due.

system.verification.V_SYS_STORAGE_OWNERS.scenario: Track waiting, active, and response occupancy through dispatch, retirement, cleanup, refresh, and response delivery.
system.verification.V_SYS_STORAGE_OWNERS.expected: The three storage categories remain capacity-independent as specified.

system.verification.V_BASE_POLICY.scenario: Compare row-retention and cleanup behavior under configured page-policy values.
system.verification.V_BASE_POLICY.expected: The default is open_page; close_page behavior remains configurable without loss of request ownership.

system.verification.V_R7.scenario: Run identical traffic under open_page and close_page parameter values.
system.verification.V_R7.expected: Open-page retains serviced rows; close-page reserves cleanup until legal PRE and blocks dispatch during cleanup.

system.verification.V_CONSTRAINT_5.scenario: Observe admission, dispatch, and service ordering under row-hit and row-miss traffic.
system.verification.V_CONSTRAINT_5.expected: FIFO policy is retained independent of row-hit preference.

system.verification.V_SYS_ORDERING.scenario: Place older row misses and conflicts ahead of newer row hits and vary timing stalls.
system.verification.V_SYS_ORDERING.expected: Dispatch and completion follow acceptance order despite different command setup costs.

system.verification.V_BASE_SEQUENCE.scenario: Dispatch a complete request, change host inputs afterward, and stall each setup and final command.
system.verification.V_BASE_SEQUENCE.expected: Captured active payload survives until final commit; dispatch/dequeue and retirement remain distinct; only committed operations change row state.

system.verification.V_BASE_MODULARITY.scenario: Review future decomposition contracts and declared functional interfaces.
system.verification.V_BASE_MODULARITY.expected: Request storage, selection, sequencing, timing, and functional memory are independently verifiable and distinct.

system.verification.V_R3.scenario: Service closed-bank, row-hit, and row-conflict reads and writes while timing-blocking each candidate and raising refresh pending.
system.verification.V_R3.expected: Only NOP, ACT, PRE, READ, WRITE, and REF semantics are used; one command at most commits per edge; setup does not retire; blocked candidates remain stable.

system.verification.V_R4.scenario: Inspect future architecture contracts and interface-level verification intent.
system.verification.V_R4.expected: Required behavioral roles are independently contractable with structural top-level integration only; no single owner contract contains all required functions.

execution.verification.V_EXEC_COMMANDS.scenario: Run closed, hit, and conflict sequences with multi-cycle timing stalls and refresh pending transitions.
execution.verification.V_EXEC_COMMANDS.expected: Committed trace is ACT-access, access, or PRE-ACT-access as applicable; setup never retires and no candidate changes while blocked.

execution.verification.V_EXEC_CLEANUP.scenario: Retire accesses under both page policies and raise refresh during close-page cleanup.
